Regular Council Meeting CITY OF SOLANA BEACH
ACTION AGENDA
The Action Agenda of the City Council Meeting is a document provided immediately following the Council Meeting in order for staff and the public to be aware of the business transacted and actions taken by Council. This is a preliminary draft and not a public record. The meeting's legal record is the Minutes approved by the City Council.
SOLANA BEACH CITY COUNCIL
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY and PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY
JOINT
REGULAR
MEETING
WEDNESDAY, JUNE 27, 2007
06:00 P.M.
CITY COUNCIL CHAMBERS
635 S. HIGHWAY 101
SOLANA BEACH, CALIFORNIA
The City Council acts as the City of Solana Beach Redevelopment Agency and the Public Financing Authority.
NOTICE
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, persons with a disability may request an agenda in appropriate alternative formats as required by Section 202 of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990. Any person with a disability who requires a modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should direct such request to the City Clerk's office at (858) 720-2400 at least 48 hours before the meeting.
As a courtesy to all meeting attendees, please set cellular phones and pagers to silent mode and engage in conversations outside the Council Chambers.
The Regular Meetings of the City Council are scheduled for 2nd and 4th Wednesdays and are broadcast live on Cox Communications, Channel 19, and Time Warner, Channel 24.
A full City Council agenda packet with all backup information is available at City Hall and the Solana Beach branch of the San Diego County Library the Friday before each Council meeting and on the web at www.ci.solana-beach.ca.us .

LESA HEEBNER, MAYOR

Claudia Carillo, SDGE, stated that in order to meet peak demand small actions would be required to reduce current energy usage and she suggested ways to conserve energy.
Vicki Cypherd displayed a sign that was nailed to a palm tree that advertised German Shepherds and asked what the policy was for signs posted.
David Ott, City Manager, stated signs are prohibited on all public property including the right of way and suggested that residents report it to Code Enforcement to handle and to not remove the sign themselves.

Council announced community events.

PUBLIC HEARINGS continued: (Items 5-9)
This portion of the agenda provides citizens an opportunity to express their views on a specific issue as required by law after proper noticing by submitting a speaker slip to the City Clerk (located on the back table). After considering all of the evidence, including written materials and oral testimony, the City Council must make a decision supported by findings and the findings must be supported by substantial evidence in the record. An applicant or designee for a private development/business project, for which the public hearing is being held, is allotted a total of fifteen minutes to speak, as per SBMC 2.04.210. A portion of the fifteen minutes may be saved to respond to those who speak in opposition. All other speakers have three minutes each. Please be aware of the three-minute timer light on the Council Dais.
5.
Fiscal Year 2007-08 Resolution of City Fees. (File No. 0390-20)
A.
Receive report
B.
Adopt Resolution 2007-067 establishing a schedule of fees and charges for City services.
Item 5 Document
Steve Didier, Management Analyst, presented a PowerPoint presentation.
Eric Johnson, RCS (Revenue and Cost Specialists), reviewed the methodology used to determine the proposed cost of City services.
Mayor Heebner opened the public hearing.
Walter Oliver asked if the new business certificate initial fee would affect all contractors such as window washers, handy people, and businesses who may only have one client in Solana Beach , that the fee would be passed onto their customers, that there were other ways to generate recovery of costs such as an increase in vacation rentals, and suggested that Council look at it further.
Council discussion ensued regarding that fact that all cities charge a fee for all business certificates and licenses, confirmed that the fee of the initial business certificate would be $70.00 for a landscaping company that is a registered business or incorporated who has only client once a week, that kids cutting yards would not be assessed the fee, and that the line has to be drawn somewhere.
Gordon Johns said that the Budget and Finance Committee supported the fee study and that the fee increases would get the City on track for cost recovery after 10 years of inattention.
MOTION: Moved by Roberts and seconded by Nichols to close the public hearing. Motion carried unanimously.
MOTION: Moved by Roberts and seconded by Campbell. Motion carried unanimously.
Council discussion continued regarding yard services, that it was a public safety issue to be aware of who is doing business in Solana Beach, fee waivers, and the difference in fees for resident and non-resident programs based on other cities' standards.
6.

Adopt Resolution No. 2007-091 approving EDCO's rate review request increasing commercial solid waste rates for FY 2007-08 in accordance with the Franchise Agreement.

Council and staff discussion ensued regarding setting public hearing for July 11th, that Mayor Heebner and Councilmember Nichols would assess the Coastal Rail Trail’s tree and landscaping status, and to obtain organic material subsidized by SDG&E.
10.5
Condo-Hotel. (File No. 0610-10)
A.
Give Staff direction as to whether to process a regulatory ordinance to develop a ban of the condo-hotel ownership method for hotels in the Commercial Zone or allowing for restrictions on condo-hotel uses.
Item 10.5 Document
MOTION: Moved by Roberts and seconded by Nichols move forward with process to ban. Motion carried unanimously.
Council and staff discussion ensued regarding condohotels being too complex of an issue for small city, that land is scarce and should be used for other things, how to enforce, prohibiting the fractional use of these properties, that the City Attorney will review all zoning and general plan issues for any conflicts, that a prohibition would be presented in a public hearing and the CEQA process, that the City may be the first to prohibit rather than impose restrictions, that it would be more of an inforcement issue than the City could provide for, that the Local Coastal Plan should be included in a prohibition, and that the City could take a leadership role in this issue, and the concern of how they affect the immediate community.
